Cluster inference used Z>2.3 with corrected cluster threshold p=.05.

Cue presentation and craving measurements

description.value: Participants viewed blocks of smoking and neutral cues while allowing themselves to crave or resisting the urge to smoke, with rest periods.

Participants viewed standardized pictures depicting people smoking and smoking-related objects such as cigarette packages and ashtrays. In the Crave condition they were instructed to allow themselves to crave; in the Resist condition they were instructed to resist the urge to smoke using any helpful strategy.

Participants viewed standardized pictures of people engaged in neutral activities and neutral objects such as pencils and dishes, matched to the smoking-related images. These images served as the comparison condition during both the Crave and Resist scans.

During the first fMRI stimulus presentation, participants viewed smoking-related and neutral pictures in alternating blocks and were instructed to allow themselves to crave when viewing smoking-related pictures. They rated craving after each block.

During the second fMRI stimulus presentation, participants viewed smoking-related and neutral pictures in alternating blocks and were instructed to resist the urge to smoke when viewing smoking-related pictures by any means they found helpful. They rated craving after each block.

spans.text: Stimuli were presented in a block design

stimuli.value: Standardized pictures of people smoking or engaged in neutral activities, and smoking-related or neutral objects.

spans.text: Each block was followed by a 6 second screen with a self-rating of craving using a hand-pad fitted on to the right hand.

instructions.value: Participants completed two back-to-back fMRI stimulus presentations. During the first, they were instructed to “allow yourself to crave when you see the smoking related pictures.” During the second, they were instructed to “resist the urge to smoke when you see the smoking pictures by any means you find helpful.” They also rated craving after each block using a hand-pad.

value: Self-rated craving on a 0–10 scale after each block; mean craving ratings were reported for the crave and resist scans.

Post-scan structured interview identifying the strategies used to resist craving; distraction was used by 40%, contemplating adverse effects of smoking by 22%, and contemplating benefits of quitting by 18%.
